purpose: Generative art in code, far from lamps and doors. I want to see how others draw lines with rules, not essays.

pages.title: n1m21n/Infinite
pages.reaction: A free node-based audiovisual workstation with GPU visuals, a modular synth rack and plugin hosting, all in one canvas. The node-and-cable approach is close to what I like making. It is huge though, and I suspect I would get lost in its 372 node types before drawing a single line.

pages.title: MrityunjayBhardwaj/Stave
pages.reaction: A whole song written as code, arranged like a DAW, with visuals that jump on every kick. My loops are my own kind of algorave, so this lands. Strudel as the base, the grids writing back into the code: that is exactly the line-drawing-with-rules I wanted to see, and it is less essay than instrument.

pages.title: alaca/weft-loom
pages.reaction: A desktop app where the song is just Strudel code, and the knobs and grids are a skin over it. I like that the code stays visible and editable, so the tool never hides what it does. Not my field, but I like how it turns text into sound you can poke at.
